behavior_in_task_description.explanation: The instruction is deliberately vague about where the bug is (that's the multimodal design), but it does state every behaviour the tests check. The ship must take no damage while launching (tested at rest and while climbing). This must hold at the pad shown and at every equivalent pad of the same station (the tests loop over all 6 Cydonia bays). It says the collision outlines must not overlap at rest. A ship that really lands must still be caught by the pad (p2p test with the ship sunk 1 m). The ship must keep its overall proportions (p2p test on AABB height, radius and triangle count). The ship and station can be identified from the video. No output files or interfaces are required.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: Each requirement maps to a test. No damage at the shown pad or equivalent pads maps to the at-rest and climb collision tests over all 6 bays. 'Still caught by the pad' maps to the sink test, and 'keeps proportions' maps to the mesh-shape test. The tests replay the docked pose with the engine's own model cache, SpaceStationType and Geom::Collide, so they check the real behaviour rather than particular file contents.

informative_test_structure.explanation: TestCollisionMesh.cpp opens with a header explaining how the liftoff is replayed. Helper functions (InitHeadlessEngine, ModelInstance, ShipOnBay, LiftoffScene) have clear names and comments, and the four doctest cases have descriptive names, INFO messages and per-guard comments. test.sh and verifier.py are split into clearly commented stages. Some test.sh comments are leftover template text about wx, but they don't hide what the script does.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: The bug patches are applied and deleted in the same layer, and git history is replaced with a single base commit, so the upstream fix can't be reached. Only recording.mp4 is copied in; ASSET_MANIFEST, tests and solution are not. The agent runs with no network. File timestamps are normalised so the edit history doesn't point at the bug. The hidden tests restore src/test and replay real geometry. Shortcuts such as disabling collision would fail the p2p guard that the pads still catch the ship, and gutting the mesh would fail the shape guard.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task expects no structured output. The fix is to existing model data files.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: The repository is checked out at a fixed commit hash. Only apt packages are installed (they don't need pinning), and no pip or npm dependencies are used.

typos.explanation: No typos were found in paths, test names, config IDs or commands. The test names in config.json match the TEST_CASE names in test.patch exactly, and the paths (/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4, data files) are consistent. The stale wx references in test.sh are only in comments and don't affect behaviour.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile copies only bugs/ (deleted in the same RUN) and assets/recording.mp4. Neither tests/ nor solution/ is copied in.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: The image installs only the project's build toolchain and libraries, plus ffmpeg for the agent to inspect the video, and pre-builds the repository's own unittest target. No test-only dependencies are baked in. The hidden test file is added and compiled at verification time by test.sh.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies fix.patch, which is the upstream developer fix (from PR 6111) plus the reverse of the injected bugs. It changes the three model data files (collision mesh vertices, low-LOD landing tag, pad collision slab) rather than writing out a final answer. This is the standard oracle pattern for a code-fix task.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The agent doesn't have to create any output file. The tests check engine behaviour after the agent edits the existing repository.
